"LA ESPADA CELESTIAL
ENCARGO MAESTRO DEFINITIVO PARA IA GAME LAB
RPG DE FANTASÍA ÉPICA — OBJETIVO: ASPIRAR A GOTY
INSTRUCCIÓN PRINCIPAL:
Quiero que desarrolles LA ESPADA CELESTIAL, un videojuego RPG de fantasía medieval, acción, aventura, exploración y criaturas coleccionables. No quiero una simple demostración, una maqueta, una presentación, una biblia de diseño ni un escenario con botones decorativos. Quiero un videojuego real, jugable, funcional, profundo, original y profesional.
La ambición es crear un título capaz de competir algún día entre los mejores videojuegos del mundo y aspirar al premio GOTY (Game of the Year).
No afirmes que el juego ha ganado o merece un premio sin haberlo conseguido. El GOTY es nuestro objetivo de excelencia, no una promesa.
Debes trabajar sobre las capacidades reales de IA Game Lab, inspeccionar el proyecto existente y utilizar las herramientas disponibles para construir el juego. No inventes funciones que la plataforma no pueda ejecutar. Si algo no es posible, explica la limitación y desarrolla la mejor alternativa técnica.
---
1. IDENTIDAD DEL VIDEOJUEGO
Nombre: LA ESPADA CELESTIAL.
Género: RPG de acción, fantasía medieval, aventura, exploración, combate y colección de criaturas.
Plataforma prioritaria: Android.
Orientación: Horizontal.
Idioma: Español de España.
Estética: Fantasía medieval cinematográfica con personalidad anime, escenarios detallados, iluminación espectacular, personajes originales y efectos visuales de alta calidad.
Inspiración: La profundidad de los grandes RPG, la libertad de exploración de las aventuras clásicas y la emoción de coleccionar criaturas, sin copiar personajes, diseños, música, historias ni propiedades intelectuales existentes.
El juego debe tener identidad propia y ser reconocible por su universo, personajes, criaturas, música y dirección artística.
---
2. OBJETIVO DE CALIDAD: NIVEL GOTY
Diseña y desarrolla el juego siguiendo estándares de excelencia en:
Jugabilidad.
Combate.
Historia.
Personajes.
Mundo.
Exploración.
Diseño artístico.
Música y sonido.
Animaciones.
Inteligencia artificial.
Interfaz y controles.
Rendimiento.
Accesibilidad.
Profundidad de sistemas.
Originalidad.
Cada sistema debe aportar algo al conjunto.
No quiero cantidad sin calidad.
No quiero un mundo enorme vacío, enemigos repetidos, misiones genéricas ni habilidades que no tengan utilidad.
Quiero una experiencia memorable.
---
3. UNIVERSO E HISTORIA
El mundo está formado por regiones conectadas por una historia épica.
Región inicial: VALDORIA
Una tierra de aldeas, bosques, praderas, ríos, montañas, ruinas y antiguas civilizaciones.
Aquí comienza la aventura.
Región de DRAKMOR
Territorios volcánicos, fortalezas, ciudades devastadas, bosques oscuros y criaturas corrompidas.
Región de KANSORDORE
Templos celestiales, ciudades antiguas, bibliotecas prohibidas, dimensiones alternativas y misterios relacionados con el origen del mundo.
Elementos fundamentales de la historia
La Gema Celestial.
La Jarra de Origen.
La Lágrima de la Primera Brasa.
La Profecía de Jugador Cero.
La Convergencia Absoluta.
El Despertar.
La Resonancia.
El Velo.
La Ruptura.
La Ascensión.
Construye una historia original, coherente y emocionante, con misterios, revelaciones, conflictos, decisiones, consecuencias, personajes memorables y un final satisfactorio.
No reveles todos los misterios al principio.
La historia debe desarrollarse mediante acontecimientos jugables, diálogos, exploración y escenas cinematográficas.
---
4. PROTAGONISTA
Crear un protagonista personalizable.
Permitir configurar, según las posibilidades técnicas:
Nombre.
Rostro.
Pelo.
Color de pelo.
Ropa.
Armadura.
Casco.
Accesorios.
Armas.
Estadísticas
Vida.
Maná.
Resistencia.
Fuerza.
Defensa.
Velocidad.
Inteligencia.
Suerte.
Cada atributo debe tener efectos medibles.
El equipamiento debe modificar las estadísticas y, cuando sea viable, la apariencia del personaje.
Crear animaciones diferenciadas de reposo, caminar, correr, atacar, esquivar, bloquear, recibi
"

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review. Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests. ## Wiki index - [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md) - [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md) - [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md) - [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md) - [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md) - [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md) ## Main project file The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml). Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md) aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job. Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue. Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run. ## Shell timing When writing shell scripts, always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands. Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command; the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in interactive shell commands. ## Ideas Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`. ## Links in handoffs When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use the `codex://threads/` URL format. When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days. ## OpenCode GitHub Actions To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user. Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation. The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward. When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status. Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`, which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit. Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account. Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only. Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota. Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound. Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries. Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save. Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker. To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`, then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` to discover the host and port and SSH with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper. When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when live log evidence can be collected. For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ``` The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from `_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while inspecting the runner. ## Mac SSH access The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as: ```sh ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running. ## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub ``` For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and use the same key: ```sh ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \ -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \ -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \ -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment. The OMG workflow is: **idea → issue → playable project.** If you believe software should start with a sentence instead of a sprint plan, [⭐ star the repository](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub) and try it.
**Built with GitHub Actions, OpenCode, shared skills, and unreasonable optimism.** 😏

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build **LA ESPADA CELESTIAL**, a real playable Spanish-language epic fantasy action RPG for Android/browser, with 3D exploration, combat, story, character customization, creature collection, UI, audio, and GOTY-level polish ambition.
- The repo was nearly empty, so the assistant is building a browser game from scratch with Three.js/Vite rather than a design document.

## Requirements
- Name: **LA ESPADA CELESTIAL**; genre: medieval fantasy action RPG, adventure, exploration, creature collection.
- Priority platform: Android; horizontal orientation; Spanish from Spain.
- Cinematic medieval fantasy with anime personality, original characters/world/music, no copied IP.
- Regions: **VALDORIA**, **DRAKMORE**, **KANSORDORE**.
- Required story concepts: Gema Celestial, Jarra de Origen, Lágrima de la Primera Brasa, Profecía de Jugador Cero, Convergencia Absoluta, Despertar, Resonancia, Velo, Ruptura, Ascensión.
- Customizable protagonist: name, face/hair/skin/outfit/armor/weapon/accessories; stats with measurable effects.
- Real gameplay, not mockups/decorative buttons; no false claims of awards.
- Mobile touch controls, safe areas, responsive layout.
- User prompt was truncated mid-protagonist animation list.

## Decisions
- Use **Three.js 0.187.0 + Vite 8.3.5**, procedural 3D assets, no external game IP assets.
- Build three compact, dense regions with sequential quests, bosses, wild creature capture, gear/loot, dialogue, leveling, codex, minimap, save/continue.
- Use procedural WebAudio music/SFX, local TTF fonts, HTML/CSS HUD, mobile joystick + action buttons.
- Implement full story arc through all three regions and an ending rather than a single demo area.
- Save game via `localStorage` key `la-espada-celestial-save-v1`; settings key `la-espada-celestial-settings-v1`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected repo: only README, workflow, agent skills, start/capture scripts; no game code.
- Created `package.json` with Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.
- Installed `three@0.187.0` and `vite@8.3.5`; `node_modules` present.
- Downloaded bundled fonts to `public/fonts/`: Cinzel 400/700/900, Alegreya Sans 400/700.
- Created full `index.html` with loading, title, character creator, intro, HUD, dialogue, journal/menu, modal, ending, mobile controls, rotate prompt.
- Created `src/styles.css` with complete responsive cinematic UI, HUD, menus, creator, mobile controls, animations.
- Created `src/game/data.js`: attributes, origins, appearance options, regions, quests, creatures, items, lore, intro slides, ending text, save key.
- Created `src/core/utils.js`: math/noise/RNG, canvas textures, sprite helpers, portrait SVGs, disposal/projection.
- Created `src/core/audio.js`: procedural music moods, reverb, ambience, SFX.
- Created `src/core/input.js`: keyboard, mouse drag/click, touch joystick, action buttons.
- Created `src/game/character.js`: procedural hero rig with customization, sword, cape, hair styles, animation, creature meshes.
- Created `src/game/world.js`: three procedural regions, terrain, paths, grass/trees/rocks/flowers, sky, water/lava, particles, village/ruins/fortress/temple, rifts/seals/portals/altars, NPCs, chests, lore stones, markers, interactables, region update/dispose.
- Created `src/game/enemies.js`: corrupt/wraith/golem/boss meshes, AI, telegraphs, boss phases, damage/death.
- Created `src/game/player.js`: movement, camera-relative control, collision, sprint/block/dodge/combos/heavy attacks, stamina/mana, potions, stats/gear/buffs/XP.
- Created `src/game/vfx.js`: slash, sparks, shockwave, heal, block, capture, beam, dust, projectiles.
- Created `src/game/story.js`: Spanish dialogue for Lira, Orin, Testigo, bosses, altars, ending, companion flavor text.
- Attempted to create `src/game/game.js`; **the write failed due to output length**, so the file likely does not exist or is incomplete.

### Active
- Writing `src/game/game.js`, the main orchestrator, from scratch in smaller chunks.

### Blocked
- `game.js` not yet written; `src/main.js` not yet written; game cannot run/build yet.

## Next Move
1. Create `src/game/game.js` in multiple smaller writes/edits. Implement:
   - renderer/composer/camera/resize/postprocessing;
   - title 3D scene with giant celestial sword, orbit camera, particles;
   - creator preview renderer + character creation state/UI;
   - intro slides and screen transitions;
   - new game/continue/save/load/autosave;
   - world initialization, player, ambient enemies, wild creatures, bosses;
   - combat integration/VFX/projectiles/damage numbers;
   - quest progression across Valdoria → Drakmore → Kansordore;
   - dialogue typewriter/choices;
   - interaction prompts, capture/resonance hold, companion summon;
   - HUD/minimap/map/journal/equipment/creatures/settings menus;
   - ending screen, death/respawn, travel fade.
2. Create `src/main.js` importing and instantiating `App`.
3. Fix known bug in `world.js` grass height condition: `if (y < regionId === 'valdoria' ? -1.1 : -1.5)` needs parentheses: `if (y < (regionId === 'valdoria' ? -1.1 : -1.5))`.
4. Run `npm run build`; fix syntax/runtime errors.
5. Start app on port 3000/3002 and test with Playwright; capture desktop/mobile screenshots and inspect.
6. Iterate visuals/gameplay; add any missing CSS (e.g. damage flash, modal actions).
7. Run smoke tests and finalize README/report without claiming awards.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game/game.js`: missing/incomplete main orchestrator; highest priority.
- `src/main.js`: missing entry point.
- `index.html`: complete DOM/UI contract and IDs expected by `game.js`.
- `src/styles.css`: complete UI styling; add missing classes as needed.
- `src/game/data.js`: canonical data for regions, quests, creatures, items, lore.
- `src/game/world.js`: region builder/interactables; fix grass conditional bug.
- `src/game/player.js`: player stats/combat/equipment APIs.
- `src/game/enemies.js`: enemy/boss APIs.
- `src/game/vfx.js`: VFX and `Projectile`.
- `src/game/story.js`: dialogue scripts.
- `src/core/input.js`: action events/camera/touch.
- `src/core/audio.js`: `AudioEngine` moods/SFX.
- `src/game/character.js`: hero/creature mesh builders.
- `src/core/utils.js`: portraits/noise/texture helpers.
- `package.json`: scripts/build config.

## Important Context
- `game.js` write was rejected with `output token limit (stop reason: length) was reached`; break it into several smaller `write`/`edit` calls.
- Expected UI IDs are already in `index.html` (e.g. `#game-canvas`, `#title-screen`, `#creator-screen`, `#hud`, `#menu-content`, `#dialogue-screen`, `#ending-screen`, `#mobile-controls`).
- Existing `world.js` API: `buildWorld(scene, regionId, quest, quality)` returns world with `heightAt`, `colliders`, `interactables`, `poi`, `creatureSpawns`, `spawn`, `bossTrigger`, `setRiftCleansed`, `setSealBroken`, `openPortal`, `update`, `dispose`.
- Existing `Player` API: `update`, `tryAttack`, `tryDodge`, `usePotion`, `takeDamage`, `reviveAtSpawn`, `addXp`, `equip`, `applyCreatureBuffs`, `recomputeStats`, `derived`, `equipment`.
- Existing `Enemy` API: constructor `{type, region, x, z, elite, boss, chapter, name, id, y, bossType}`, `update(dt, game)`, `takeDamage`, `hpRatio`, `alive`, `capturable`.
- `Enemy` calls game hooks: `onEnemyAggro`, `onBossPhase`, `onEnemyKilled`, `onEnemyWeakened`, `spawnEnemyProjectile`, `spawnShockwave`, `spawnSlashTrail`, `damagePlayer`, `shake`, `audio`, `scene`, `world`, `player`, `time`.
- `Projectile` constructor `{x,y,z,dir,damage,color,speed,radius,life,hostile,owner}`; update calls `destroy`.
- `AudioEngine` requires a user gesture via `await audio.init()`; methods include `setMood`, `update`, `ui`, `confirm`, `swing`, `heavySwing`, `hit`, `hurt`, `dodge`, `block`, `potion`, `capture`, `quest`, `level`, `portal`, `death`, `bossRoar`, `arrow`, `chest`, `setVolume`.
- `Input` emits `action(name, 'down'|'up')`, `camera(dx,dy)`, `zoom`, `pause`; actions include `attack`, `heavy`, `dodge`, `block`, `interact`, `resonance`, `companion`, `potion`, `menu`, `pause`, `lock`, `map`, `sprint`.
- `Player` expects `game.cameraYaw`, `game.input`, `game.world`, `game.scene`, `game.audio`, `game.time`, `game.toast`, `game.spawnSlashTrail`, `game.hitEnemiesInArc`, `game.findAttackTarget`, `game.damageNumber`, `game.spawnHitSparks`, `game.spawnHealEffect`, `game.spawnBlockEffect`, `game.flashDamage`, `game.shake`, `game.perfectBlock`, `game.updateHud`, `game.onPlayerAttack`, `game.onPlayerDeath`, `game.onLevelUp`.
- Assets are fully procedural; no external GLB needed.
- Current git state: initial repo had only one commit; all new files are untracked/uncommitted.
- Avoid claiming the game has won or deserves GOTY.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build **LA ESPADA CELESTIAL**, a playable Spanish-language epic fantasy action RPG for Android/browser with 3D exploration, combat, story, character customization, creature collection, UI, audio, and polished presentation.

## Requirements
- Name: **LA ESPADA CELESTIAL**; medieval fantasy action RPG with adventure, exploration, and creature collection.
- Priority platform: Android; horizontal orientation; Spanish from Spain.
- Cinematic medieval fantasy with anime personality; original characters/world/music; no copied IP.
- Regions: **VALDORIA**, **DRAKMORE**, **KANSORDORE**.
- Story concepts required: Gema Celestial, Jarra de Origen, Lágrima de la Primera Brasa, Profecía de Jugador Cero, Convergencia Absoluta, Despertar, Resonancia, Velo, Ruptura, Ascensión.
- Customizable protagonist: name, face/hair/skin/outfit/armor/weapon/accessories; stats with measurable effects.
- Real gameplay, not mockups/decorative buttons; no false claims of awards.
- Mobile touch controls, safe areas, responsive layout.
- User prompt was truncated mid-protagonist animation list.

## Decisions
- Use **Three.js 0.187.0 + Vite 8.3.5**, procedural 3D assets, no external game IP assets.
- Three compact, dense regions with sequential quests, bosses, wild creature capture, gear/loot, dialogue, leveling, codex, minimap, save/continue.
- Procedural WebAudio music/SFX, local TTF fonts, HTML/CSS HUD, mobile joystick + action buttons.
- Implement full story arc through all three regions and an ending rather than a single demo area.
- Save game via `localStorage` key `la-espada-celestial-save-v1`; settings key `la-espada-celestial-settings-v1`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Repo inspection; `package.json` created with Vite scripts and Three.js dependency; dependencies installed.
- Bundled fonts downloaded to `public/fonts/` (Cinzel 400/700/900, Alegreya Sans 400/700).
- Full `index.html` UI contract created: loading, title, creator, intro, HUD, dialogue, journal/menu, modal, ending, mobile controls, rotate prompt.
- `src/styles.css` created with responsive cinematic UI; added `#app.is-hurt` damage-flash styling.
- `src/game/data.js`, `src/core/utils.js`, `src/core/audio.js`, `src/core/input.js`, `src/game/character.js`, `src/game/world.js`, `src/game/enemies.js`, `src/game/player.js`, `src/game/vfx.js`, `src/game/story.js` all created.
- Fixed `world.js` grass height bug: now `if (y < (regionId === 'valdoria' ? -1.1 : -1.5)) continue;`.
- Patched `vfx.js` `shockwave` to accept optional `y` and position the ring at terrain height.
- **`src/game/game.js` fully written** (~2,000 lines) with:
  - renderer/camera/resize, title 3D sword scene, creator preview renderer;
  - character creator UI, derived stats, intro slides;
  - new game/continue/save/load/autosave, quest state per region;
  - world loading, player creation, enemy/creature spawning, boss triggers;
  - combat integration, VFX wrappers, projectiles, damage numbers, lock-on;
  - dialogue typewriter/choices, interactions, chests, lore;
  - resonance capture, companion summon/follow/attacks;
  - HUD/minimap/target/boss UI, journal/equipment/creatures/map/settings menus;
  - region travel, death/respawn, ending, New Game+.
- **`src/main.js` created** importing `App` and booting with error fallback.
- Removed duplicate stylesheet `<link>` from `index.html` (CSS now imported by `main.js`).
- `npm run build` succeeds: 18 modules, JS 788.92 kB, CSS 46.54 kB; only chunk-size warning.
- Dev server launched in background on port 3000.

### Active
- Runtime/browser testing and visual verification. Playwright browser launch currently blocked by missing Chromium executable.
- Need to verify title → creator → intro → gameplay, menus, combat, capture, quests, travel, ending.

### Blocked
- `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3000` fails: `Browser "chromium" is not installed; expected executable at /home/runner/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome`.
- System Chromium exists at `/usr/bin/chromium`, `/usr/bin/chromium-browser`, and `/usr/bin/google-chrome`, but Playwright CLI expects its own cache path.
- Possible next fix: run `playwright-cli install-browser chromium` or launch system Chromium directly with `--headless --screenshot`.

## Next Move
1. Install Playwright Chromium (`playwright-cli install-browser chromium`) or use system Chromium headless for screenshots.
2. Open the game and capture desktop + mobile screenshots of title, creator, intro, gameplay/HUD.
3. Check browser console for runtime errors; fix any JS/runtime issues.
4. Exercise gameplay: movement, combat, rift cleansing, boss spawn/kill, altar, portal travel, creature resonance, companion, menu tabs, save/continue, death/respawn, ending.
5. Verify touch layout at landscape mobile size and add any missing CSS.
6. Create smoke tests (`tests/smoke.mjs` is referenced by `npm test` but not yet created).
7. Update README with real feature description and controls; avoid award/GOTY claims.
8. Commit final changes (all files currently untracked/uncommitted).

## Relevant Files
- `src/game/game.js`: main orchestrator; all game flow, UI, combat hooks, quests, menus, save/load.
- `src/main.js`: entry point booting `App`.
- `index.html`: DOM contract and expected element IDs.
- `src/styles.css`: complete UI styling plus damage-flash CSS.
- `src/game/world.js`: procedural regions, interactables, POIs, bosses, portals, quest visuals.
- `src/game/player.js`: stats, combat, movement, equipment, potions, XP.
- `src/game/enemies.js`: enemy/boss meshes and AI; calls many `game.*` hooks.
- `src/game/vfx.js`: slash/sparks/shockwave/heal/capture/beam and `Projectile`.
- `src/game/data.js`: canonical regions, quests, creatures, items, lore, intro/ending text.
- `src/game/story.js`: Spanish dialogue scripts.
- `src/core/input.js`: keyboard/touch input and action events.
- `src/core/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio moods/SFX.
- `src/game/character.js`: procedural hero/creature meshes and animation.
- `src/core/utils.js`: noise, textures, portraits, projection helpers.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts (`dev`, `build`, `preview`, `test`).

## Important Context
- `npm run build` passes; no syntax errors currently known.
- Playwright CLI is available at `/usr/local/bin/playwright-cli`; its Chromium is not installed.
- System Chromium binaries are available at `/usr/bin/chromium`, `/usr/bin/chromium-browser`, `/usr/bin/google-chrome`.
- `game.js` uses `this.creator` for creator state, `this.player.allocated` for saved stat allocation.
- Save data includes quests, inventory, collection, active creature, lore, chests, stats, equipment, appearance, region, level/XP/gold/potions.
- `game.js` hooks expected by `Enemy`: `onEnemyAggro`, `onBossPhase`, `onEnemyKilled`, `onEnemyWeakened`, `spawnEnemyProjectile`, `spawnShockwave`, `spawnSlashTrail`, `damagePlayer`, `shake`, `audio`, `scene`, `world`, `player`, `time`.
- `game.js` hooks expected by `Player`: `cameraYaw`, `input`, `world`, `scene`, `audio`, `time`, `toast`, `spawnSlashTrail`, `hitEnemiesInArc`, `findAttackTarget`, `damageNumber`, `spawnHitSparks`, `spawnHealEffect`, `spawnBlockEffect`, `flashDamage`, `shake`, `perfectBlock`, `updateHud`, `onPlayerAttack`, `onPlayerDeath`, `onLevelUp`.
- Assets are fully procedural; no external GLB needed.
- Git state: initial repo had one commit; all game files are untracked/uncommitted.
- Do not claim the game has won or deserves GOTY.

"LA ESPADA CELESTIAL
ENCARGO MAESTRO DEFINITIVO PARA IA GAME LAB
RPG DE FANTASÍA ÉPICA — OBJETIVO: ASPIRAR A GOTY
INSTRUCCIÓN PRINCIPAL:
Quiero que desarrolles LA ESPADA CELESTIAL, un videojuego RPG de fantasía medieval, acción, aventura, exploración y criaturas coleccionables. No quiero una simple demostración, una maqueta, una presentación, una biblia de diseño ni un escenario con botones decorativos. Quiero un videojuego real, jugable, funcional, profundo, original y profesional.
La ambición es crear un título capaz de competir algún día entre los mejores videojuegos del mundo y aspirar al premio GOTY (Game of the Year).
No afirmes que el juego ha ganado o merece un premio sin haberlo conseguido. El GOTY es nuestro objetivo de excelencia, no una promesa.
Debes trabajar sobre las capacidades reales de IA Game Lab, inspeccionar el proyecto existente y utilizar las herramientas disponibles para construir el juego. No inventes funciones que la plataforma no pueda ejecutar. Si algo no es posible, explica la limitación y desarrolla la mejor alternativa técnica.
---
1. IDENTIDAD DEL VIDEOJUEGO
Nombre: LA ESPADA CELESTIAL.
Género: RPG de acción, fantasía medieval, aventura, exploración, combate y colección de criaturas.
Plataforma prioritaria: Android.
Orientación: Horizontal.
Idioma: Español de España.
Estética: Fantasía medieval cinematográfica con personalidad anime, escenarios detallados, iluminación espectacular, personajes originales y efectos visuales de alta calidad.
Inspiración: La profundidad de los grandes RPG, la libertad de exploración de las aventuras clásicas y la emoción de coleccionar criaturas, sin copiar personajes, diseños, música, historias ni propiedades intelectuales existentes.
El juego debe tener identidad propia y ser reconocible por su universo, personajes, criaturas, música y dirección artística.
---
2. OBJETIVO DE CALIDAD: NIVEL GOTY
Diseña y desarrolla el juego siguiendo estándares de excelencia en:
Jugabilidad.
Combate.
Historia.
Personajes.
Mundo.
Exploración.
Diseño artístico.
Música y sonido.
Animaciones.
Inteligencia artificial.
Interfaz y controles.
Rendimiento.
Accesibilidad.
Profundidad de sistemas.
Originalidad.
Cada sistema debe aportar algo al conjunto.
No quiero cantidad sin calidad.
No quiero un mundo enorme vacío, enemigos repetidos, misiones genéricas ni habilidades que no tengan utilidad.
Quiero una experiencia memorable.
---
3. UNIVERSO E HISTORIA
El mundo está formado por regiones conectadas por una historia épica.
Región inicial: VALDORIA
Una tierra de aldeas, bosques, praderas, ríos, montañas, ruinas y antiguas civilizaciones.
Aquí comienza la aventura.
Región de DRAKMOR
Territorios volcánicos, fortalezas, ciudades devastadas, bosques oscuros y criaturas corrompidas.
Región de KANSORDORE
Templos celestiales, ciudades antiguas, bibliotecas prohibidas, dimensiones alternativas y misterios relacionados con el origen del mundo.
Elementos fundamentales de la historia
La Gema Celestial.
La Jarra de Origen.
La Lágrima de la Primera Brasa.
La Profecía de Jugador Cero.
La Convergencia Absoluta.
El Despertar.
La Resonancia.
El Velo.
La Ruptura.
La Ascensión.
Construye una historia original, coherente y emocionante, con misterios, revelaciones, conflictos, decisiones, consecuencias, personajes memorables y un final satisfactorio.
No reveles todos los misterios al principio.
La historia debe desarrollarse mediante acontecimientos jugables, diálogos, exploración y escenas cinematográficas.
---
4. PROTAGONISTA
Crear un protagonista personalizable.
Permitir configurar, según las posibilidades técnicas:
Nombre.
Rostro.
Pelo.
Color de pelo.
Ropa.
Armadura.
Casco.
Accesorios.
Armas.
Estadísticas
Vida.
Maná.
Resistencia.
Fuerza.
Defensa.
Velocidad.
Inteligencia.
Suerte.
Cada atributo debe tener efectos medibles.
El equipamiento debe modificar las estadísticas y, cuando sea viable, la apariencia del personaje.
Crear animaciones diferenciadas de reposo, caminar, correr, atacar, esquivar, bloquear, recibi
"
